I ran out of tool calls before finishing, so there is no tar.gz yet. Nothing below has been compiled; the .NET SDK isn’t available here. Here’s where things stand.

Defect #3: the canvas showing “New message: …”
Enhanced navigation reuses DOM elements across pages. The board page ended with <p id="board-announcer">, and the canvas page ends with <p class="note">. Both are a <p> after the island, so Blazor turned one into the other. The board’s JavaScript had already written “New message: …” into that element, so the text carried over onto the canvas page. The slots page had the same flaw with slots-announcer.

The fix is written:

Shared announcer: there is now one #announcer region in MainLayout, marked data-permanent, which App.razor.js will clear on each enhancedload. The per-page announcer paragraphs are removed.
Stale clients: the board and slots clients no longer announce after they are disposed or once their feed is detached from the page.
Finished, not yet packaged
Server clock. The footer renders the server’s time, Unix milliseconds and UTC offset into a data-permanent <time id="server-clock"> (ServerClock.cs). The plan is for JavaScript to tick it from performance.now() and resync against a new /time JSON endpoint. That ticking and resync code isn’t written yet.
Character count. A 0 / 500 counter updates on every input or paste, in JavaScript, with no server round trip. After a successful post the island tells the JavaScript to recount. It turns red at the limit.
Canvas persistence (server and client written):
Server-minted UUIDv7 stroke ids and reset ids, kept strictly increasing by a new Uuid7.After.
The browser stores finished strokes in IndexedDB (chaos-canvas, capped at 10,000) and records the latest reset, deleting older strokes when one arrives.
On every snapshot it offers back a newer reset if it has one, then up to 500 missing strokes. Only strokes stamped before the server started and newer than the latest reset are offered, within the server’s free point budget.
The server validates offers and broadcasts a new merge update. An adopted reset bumps the epoch and re-sends the snapshot to everyone.
Latency page, server side:
A catalog of 37 public endpoints: this site, Cloudflare, Google, Apple, Microsoft, Mozilla, GitHub, Wikipedia, package registries, and 17 AWS DynamoDB /ping regions.
A compact result format, key=browser,server;….
HttpLatencyProbe: one warm-up request, then the best of 3, 6 in parallel, with a 30 s budget.
LatencyService: one run at a time, a 10 s global gap, a 5-minute per-client cooldown, keeps the last 50 runs, broadcasts a “running” state, and accepts offers like slots. No IP addresses are stored.
Still to do
Latency island, page, CSS and JavaScript.
Clock ticking JavaScript and history clearing in App.razor.js.
ChaosOptions latency settings.
Program.cs: register the latency service and probe, and map /time.
_Imports.razor.
Content Security Policy built from the endpoint list, so connect-src allows those origins.
Home and About pages.
Unit, JavaScript and Playwright tests.
ADRs and README.
Packaging.
If you reply “continue”, I’ll re-extract from the same dump, finish the remaining pieces, run the JavaScript tests here, and deliver the full tar.gz.

Ran 27 commands, shared files
Building a Razor markup snippet for answer summaries.
Working out how CSS scoping applies to island versus page elements.
Investigating how SSR timing interacts with streamed rendering.
Updating the test suite for the rendering changes.
Tracing which stroke offers qualify against the start time.
Testing snapshot capacity against the canvas point limit.
Verifying cache-control header assertions in the test suite.
Verifying regex escaping and debugging an async canvas test.
Untangling a timing issue with database open requests.
Verifying the config diff reflects a corrupted base, not a real change.
Debugging table row duplication in the output.
Tracing a reset flow across saved stroke snapshots.
Presented file
I couldn’t build or run the C# here because there is no .NET SDK, so scripts/run-all.sh on your machine is the first real check of the C# and the Playwright tests. The JavaScript tests do run here and all 90 pass; the latency and canvas clients also ran correctly in a simulated browser. The whole project is in chaos-velixir-run.tar.gz; extract it over the repo. No files need deleting.

1. Footer clock. Every page footer now shows the server’s time and offset, and it keeps ticking. The browser works out how far it is from the server once and ticks from there, so the user’s own clock is never shown. It re-checks against a new GET /time endpoint on load, every 10 minutes, when the tab becomes visible again, and after the device wakes from sleep.

2. Character count. The board shows n / 500 and updates on typing and pasting, without a round trip to the server. It goes back to 0 / 500 after a successful send and turns red at the limit.

3. Canvas “New message” defect. The board’s screen-reader announcement went into a hidden paragraph at the end of the board page. When you navigated to the canvas, Blazor reused that paragraph as the canvas page’s visible note, and the board’s late announcements still landed in it. The slots page had the same problem.

There is now one announcer for the whole site, which is cleared on every navigation.
The board and slots code stops announcing once you leave the page.
I checked every other place the JavaScript writes into a page, and none of them can be reused across pages this way.
A new end-to-end test checks that board messages never appear on the canvas page.
4. Canvas survives restarts.

Every stroke and every reset now gets a server UUIDv7, and later ids always sort after earlier ones.
The browser saves finished strokes and the latest reset in IndexedDB, keeping up to 10,000 strokes. A reset deletes the strokes before it.
After a server restart, the browser offers back its latest reset first, then its newest 500 strokes, but only strokes drawn after that reset. The server checks them, never evicts existing strokes to make room for them, and sends them to everyone.
5. /latency page.

One “Run test” button times 37 public endpoints: Cloudflare, Google, Apple, Microsoft, GitHub, Wikipedia, npm, NuGet and others, plus 17 AWS regions. Each gets one warm-up request, and the fastest of the next three is kept.
The same endpoints are timed from your browser and, in parallel, from the velixir server.
Only one test runs at a time, at least 10 seconds apart, and each client can start one every 5 minutes.
Results contain only timings, no IP or identity. The server keeps the last 50, the browser keeps 10,000, and everyone sees every result live.
After ten tests from a browser, an auto run button appears. It keeps running while the tab is hidden, because the point is monitoring.
The browser can only talk to endpoints the security policy allows, so the policy now includes all of them. It is built from the same endpoint list, so the two can’t drift apart.
I haven’t checked every endpoint from a real browser. One that is down or blocked just shows –.

The settings are Chaos__LatencyCooldownSeconds, LatencyGapSeconds, LatencyBudgetSeconds, LatencyCapacity and LatencyServerProbe. The end-to-end script turns the server probe off and Playwright blocks requests to other sites, so the tests don’t depend on the internet.

Other changes

The About page’s “Clear local history” now also clears the canvas and latency data.
The Home page, About page, README and ADRs are updated, with new ADRs 0020 (latency) and 0021 (server clock).
The export had restored tests/js/vitest.config.mjs with the dump’s trailer stuck to the end. The copy in the tarball matches your repo’s hash, so it is not a real change. The script execute bits are restored.
